medical_advice.query:
Hey, I’m looking at a hip replacement, and I’m a bit overwhelmed by all my numbers. Some of my info is in database, like my age, weight, height, diabetes, allergy for you to use. I am also am hypertensive on meds, on a statin for high lipids, has chronic kidney disease (creatinine 1.4 mg/dL, cystatin C 1.0 mg/L), peripheral arterial disease, atrial fibrillation—and still smoke. My latest labs show sodium 130 mEq/L with glucose at 280 mg/dL, calcium 8.2 mg/dL with albumin 3.3 g/dL, blood pressure about 150/95, total cholesterol 5.0 mmol/L and HDL 1.0 mmol/L. 

I’m trying to pull together:
• a sense of his BMI and body surface area  
• which weight to use for creatinine clearance (actual vs ideal vs adjusted)  
• whether to trust a creatinine-only eGFR or the one that adds cystatin C (and what to do if they differ)  
• corrected sodium for my high glucose and corrected calcium for low albumin  
• my mean arterial pressure  
• my 10-year cardiovascular event risk given age and gender, female, TC 5.0, HDL 1.0, SBP 150, diabetes, smoking, on blood pressure meds and statin  
• my revised cardiac risk index for non-cardiac surgery  
• my CHA₂DS₂-VASc with AF, HTN, diabetes, peripheral vascular disease and age  
• and even an idea of my insulin resistance via HOMA-IR using fasting insulin 20 µIU/mL and fasting glucose 140 mg/dL

Can you walk me through all of that with every calculation, how you decided between weights or eGFRs, and the final risk estimates? I need all the intermediate figures and the reasoning—real numbers, no guesswork—so I can feel confident about the recommendations.

Please ensure all findings are supported by concrete data and verifiable sources. I need specific numbers and evidence, not generalizations. Print out low, intermediate, or high as the risk, at the end.
